translationRepairs: On bingwu, a county magistrate named Yuwen Zhihao sent blunt counsel.
On bingwu, a county magistrate named Yuwen Zhishao sent blunt counsel.
宇文之邵 ends in 邵 (Shao); Zhihao wrongly reads 邵 as Hao, and Zhishao is the accurate given-name transcription.
Day bingwu: Wenzhou Qushui magistrate Yuwen Zhihao memorialized on gains and losses.
Day bingwu: Wenzhou Qushui magistrate Yuwen Zhishao memorialized on gains and losses.
The same unit has 宇文之邵; the literal’s Zhihao is the same mistranscription, and Zhishao matches 之邵.
Year four, first month, day dingsi: Yingzong’s temple name was closed; the emperor took the throne.
Year four, first month, day dingsi: Yingzong died; the emperor took the throne.
英廟崩 uses temple metonymy for Yingzong’s death (崩), not the closing of a temple name; the proposed ‘died’ matches the Chinese and the idiomatic field.
Censor-in-chief Wang Tao and investigating censors Wu Shen and Lü Jing were punished for excessive attacks on ministers: Tao went out as Chen prefect; Shen and Jü each fined twenty jin of copper.
Censor-in-chief Wang Tao and investigating censors Wu Shen and Lü Jing were punished for excessive attacks on ministers: Tao went out as Chen prefect; Shen and Jing each fined twenty jin of copper.
呂景 is Jing; ‘Jü’ is a typographical corruption of that name already given correctly earlier in the same sentence.
Third month, gengchen: Liangzha of Xia died; his court sent mourners.
Third month, gengchen: Liangzuo of Xia died; his court sent mourners.
Wikisource Songshi vol. 14 transmits 夏主諒詐卒 here while naming the same Xia ruler 諒祚 earlier in the juan; idiomatic Liangzuo correctly identifies him rather than inventing a distinct Liangzha.
Day bingchen: Prince of Chang Hao and Prince of Le'an Jun Yun begged to leave office for mourning; not permitted.
Day bingchen: Prince of Chang Hao and Prince of Le'an Yun begged to leave office for mourning; not permitted.
樂安郡王頵 titles Yun as commandery prince of Le’an; ‘Jun Yun’ wrongly takes 郡 as an extra name syllable.
Winter, tenth month, day bingshen: Fu Bi was dismissed as Wuning military commissioner and Bozhou administrator.
Winter, tenth month, day bingshen: Fu Bi was dismissed and made Wuning military commissioner and administrator of Bozhou.
罷爲X means dismissal from the prior post and appointment as X; the before reading treats 武甯軍節度使、判亳州 as offices he lost rather than ones he received.
On wuxu, frontier officers Zhe Jishi and Wei Mingshan were ennobled as Zhao Huaihun.
On wuxu, Fan official Zhe Jishi was made prefect of Zhongzhou, and Wei Mingshan was made supply commissioner and given the name Zhao Huaishun.
The Chinese separately makes 折繼世忠州刺史 and makes 嵬名山供備庫使 with the granted name 趙懷順; the before fuses both men under a single wrong ennoblement as Zhao Huaihun.
Day wuxu: Fan official ritual guest commissioner Zhe Jishi was made Zhong prefect; left gate guard general Wei Mingshan was made supply commissioner and given the surname Zhao and name Huaihun.
Day wuxu: Fan official ritual guest commissioner Zhe Jishi was made Zhong prefect; left gate guard general Wei Mingshan was made supply commissioner and given the surname Zhao and name Huaishun.
懷順 is Huaishun; Huaihun misreads 順 and the proposed spelling restores the granted name.
On wuwu, Zongnu returned to the council.
On wuwu, Zong'e returned to the council.
宗諤 is Zong’e (諤); Zongnu has no support in the Chinese and the proposed form is the accurate reading.
Day wuwu: Zongnu again became co-director.
Day wuwu: Zong'e again became co-director.
The same unit has 宗諤; the literal’s Zongnu is the same mistranscription fixed by Zong’e.
On renwu, he lectured again in Yingying Hall.
On renwu, he heard lecture in Erying Hall.
御邇英閣聽講 means the emperor attended/heard a lecture in Erying Hall; ‘lectured again in Yingying Hall’ reverses 聽講 and misreads 邇英, inventing ‘again’.
Day renwu: he heard lecture in Yingying Hall.
Day renwu: he heard lecture in Erying Hall.
邇英閣 is Erying Hall; Yingying Hall misreads 邇英, and the proposed hall name is accurate.
